tb21_profile.skill: Read a Python 2 script you may not modify and rewrite it as idiomatic Python 3: replace removed syntax and APIs, handle text encoding explicitly, use pathlib and configparser, do the CSV work with pandas, hit an exact stdout format, and declare version-constrained dependencies in requirements.txt or pyproject.toml.
tb21_profile.domain: Python 2-to-3 migration, the pandas/numpy scientific stack, Python packaging metadata and stdlib modernisation (pathlib, configparser).
tb21_profile.task_form: Port/modernise an existing codebase into a new file, plus a small build/packaging artefact; graded on exact printed output and on the dependency declaration.

verifier_notes: No grade overturned. Two TerminalWorld picks (tw_137513 pyproject scaffolding, tw_126385 requirements.txt environment) are FREE; both are genuinely on topic for the dependency-file half, so they are ranked 9 and 10 inside per_source with the FREE status stated, and neither appears in final_top10. Terminal-Lego's two most on-the-nose Python-2 items, task_00376 (fix a Python 2.7 threading script for Python 3) and task_01110 (SimpleHTTPServer to http.server), are both FREE and were dropped entirely.
searches: tools.py search rebench "\b(Python 2|python2|2to3|deprecat|DeprecationWarning|np\.int|np\.float|removed in|no longer supported)\b"

Fix the errors left over from a Python 2 to 3 migration of an API backend and get it running; debugging a half-done port.

notes: This is the one task of my five where the old pool holds its own. TMax-15K has a very large Python-2-to-3 migration cluster - dozens of tasks that start from a legacy Python 2 script and demand a working Python 3 replacement - and it supplies three of the final ten; most of those entries are heavier than this TB2.1 task (C extensions, gRPC, polyglot stacks), which is why they score 4 rather than 5 on task_form. CalibForge still leads, but for a different reason: it is the only corpus with the packaging half (setup.py to pyproject.toml migrations whose entry points genuinely break) and it has a large cluster of pandas CSV pipelines that must ship a working pyproject.toml, which is precisely this task's two-artefact deliverable. Its single best entry pairs both halves: a tool ported from Python 2 that then breaks on configparser percent interpolation. Terminal-Lego-15k is genuinely useful here for the first time in my set - it has a real cluster of small Python-2-idiom fixes (except-comma syntax, print-chevron, dict.keys() views, unicode handling, PEP-352 exceptions) that is exactly the edit vocabulary this task needs, though each item is tiny; two of its closest matches are FREE and were dropped. SWE-Rebench contributes cloudpickle/datadogpy/axelrod Python-2-divergence bugs and numpy deprecated-alias removal, which is real transfer. Recursive-Task-Synthesis offers only environment and packaging plumbing and nothing about porting code.
